original_question: In particular, given invertible measure preserving transformations T, S, R on a common probability space and a set A of positive measure, must there exist m, n ∈ N such that µ(A ∩ T^m A ∩ S^{m+n} A ∩ R^{m+2n} A) > 0?
target_in_paper: Section 5.3, "Transformations that do not commute": the current arXiv version’s "Special Case of Problem 21," i.e. the three-transformation linear-pattern special case of the general polynomial multiple-recurrence Problem 21.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly captures the ergodic-theoretic setting of invertible measure-preserving transformations acting on one common probability space, the positive-measure set A, the two-parameter linear pattern m, m+n, m+2n, and the intended multiple-recurrence conclusion that some fourfold intersection should have positive measure.
missing_details: The paper’s exact formulation is on a probability space (X, 𝓧, μ), with T, S, R: X → X invertible measure-preserving transformations and A ∈ 𝓧 satisfying μ(A) > 0.
A critical hidden assumption is that no commutativity is assumed here; this question appears in Section 5.3, which is specifically about transformations that do not commute.
The official formulation uses inverse iterates on sets: T^{-m}A, S^{-m-n}A, and R^{-m-2n}A, not positive powers.
The paper presents this as the special linear case of the general Problem 21 for distinct integer polynomials with zero constant term; here the underlying polynomial pattern is 0, n, 2n.
To be fully stand-alone, the quantifiers should be stated exactly as: for every measurable A with μ(A) > 0, there exist m, n ∈ ℕ such that the indicated intersection has positive μ-measure.
refined_question: Let (X, 𝓧, μ) be a probability space, and let T, S, R: X → X be invertible measure-preserving transformations, with no commutativity assumed. If A ∈ 𝓧 satisfies μ(A) > 0, must there exist m, n ∈ ℕ such that μ(A ∩ T^{-m}A ∩ S^{-m-n}A ∩ R^{-m-2n}A) > 0, where T^{-k}A := (T^k)^{-1}(A) (and similarly for S and R)?
justification: The draft clearly points to the noncommuting-transformations part of the paper: it asks about three arbitrary invertible measure-preserving transformations on one probability space and a two-parameter recurrence pattern with offsets 0, n, 2n. In the current arXiv version, the nearest official wording is the "Special Case of Problem 21," stated immediately after the general Problem 21 on distinct zero-constant-term polynomials. Section 1.2 also matters because the paper’s default framework earlier assumes commuting transformations, so the Section 5.3 context has to be made explicit in order to keep the question paper-faithful. Finally, the paper’s set formulation uses inverse iterates, so the refined version keeps T^{-m}, S^{-m-n}, and R^{-m-2n} rather than switching to positive powers. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))
